gaps.category: Taxi/VTC/ambulance and small-trucking operator duties: ROTT registers, MDS digital authorisation, tachograph and driver-hours records for autonomos hauliers
gaps.first_search: transportista autónomo obligaciones descarga tacógrafo digital tarjeta conductor ROTT MDS autorización 2026 sanciones
gaps.why: Spain has a huge population of one-truck autonomo hauliers and taxi/VTC licence-holders. Cat. 18 found no small-operator duty, but the ROTT/MDS regime (Ley 9/2013 amending LOTT), the obligation to keep tachograph data and download it every 28/90 days, and the electronic carta de porte (K16 rejected only the DeCA) were not examined.

gaps.category: Hunting-adjacent and firearms regime: armerías, tiro, guardería rural; and the Reglamento de Armas record books held by small arms dealers and collectors
gaps.first_search: armerías libro registro Intervención de Armas Guardia Civil obligaciones comunicación telemática Reglamento de Armas 2025
gaps.why: Armerías and weapons-licence holders must keep a libro-registro and report to the Guardia Civil Intervención de Armas; the pass covered hunting estates (K29) but not arms dealers, which sit in the same police-register category as scrap and second-hand dealers. Pyrotechnic retailers are also thin.

gaps.category: Self-employed and SME tax and Social Security calendars (not VeriFactu): modelo 303/130/131 quarterly filings, RETA cuota por ingresos reales, the Sistema RED / Import@ss and the new 2025-26 autonomo regularisations
gaps.first_search: regularización cuotas autónomos rendimientos reales cambio de tramo 2026 Seguridad Social obligaciones trabajadores autónomos
gaps.why: The RETA income-based contribution system (RD-ley 13/2022) forces about 3.3 million autonomos to regularise annually, and the 2026 reforms (cuota, tarifa plana, incompatibilities) hit exactly the sole-trader buyer group. The pass treated generic accounting as out of scope, but the mandatory regularisation workflow is a specific duty owed to the Seguridad Social and was not surfaced.

gaps.category: Municipal licences and registers for small premises: licencia de actividad / declaración responsable, terrazas, ruido and aforo, plus ICIO and tasa de basuras. Also taxi-style local licences and tasa de terrazas for bars and restaurants
gaps.first_search: bares y restaurantes obligaciones registro APPCC alérgenos autocontrol licencia terraza renovación ayuntamiento hostelería trazabilidad
gaps.why: Spain has an exceptionally high bar and restaurant density (about 250,000 small hospitality businesses). Their recurring duties to the ayuntamiento (terrace permit renewal, APPCC records, alergenos, health inspection, music licences, SGAE/AGEDI fees) were not covered. Cat. 20 only touched tattoo studios, driving schools, nurseries, small food producers and hunting outfitters.

gaps.category: Agriculture-sector small-operator mandates: PAC solicitud unica, SIGPAC, cuaderno digital de explotacion (RD 1054/2022), and the 2025-27 crop-nutrient registers
gaps.first_search: SITRAN comunicación movimientos ganado explotaciones ganaderas libro de registro REGA obligaciones titulares 2026 Real Decreto
gaps.why: Spain has about 800,000 farms. K27 rejected the digital farm notebook as too competitive, but the specific grounds were the large SaaS vendors. The ecoregimenes, the mandatory SIEX data transfer, the Ley 2/2025 changes on organic farming, and the fertiliser-register pairing (REGFER) are not yet joined up. The PAC solicitud unica and the livestock explotacion registers (REGA, REMO, SITRAN movement notifications) for small livestock holdings were not screened.

gaps.category: Employer-side labour and prevention duties for micro-firms: Registro Retributivo (RD 902/2020), Plan de Igualdad thresholds, canal de denuncias (Ley 2/2023), and the PRL external prevention service concertation
gaps.first_search: canal interno de información Ley 2/2023 pymes obligatorio 50 trabajadores plan de igualdad registro retributivo sanciones 2026 empresa pequeña
gaps.why: Ley 2/2023 requires a whistleblowing channel for firms of 50 or more workers, and Plan de Igualdad applies from 50. A large number of 50-250 worker family firms are therefore forced to act. Only pay transparency (K05) and the time register (K20) were covered. Small employers (under 6 workers) may also self-assume prevention, which creates a niche for a done-for-you prevention service. Cat. 26 touches manpower agencies only.

coverage.category: 31. Arms dealers (armerías), collectors and pyrotechnic retailers: Reglamento de Armas record books and Guardia Civil reporting (country-specific)
coverage.found: Art. 10 Reglamento de Armas: armeros and corredores must keep a registry of entries and exits (type, brand, model, calibre, serial, counterparty data), file a parte de venta with the Intervención de Armas (art. 52), report electronically without undue delay (RD 726/2020), hand over books on closure; shops selling arms as a side line also keep an entries/exits book (art. 56). RD 653/2023 touched the Registro Nacional de Armas. Guardia Civil is renewing its Intervención de Armas system and uses NOTIFIC@. Two searches found no Spanish vertical software for armerías (only generic TPV). Pyrotechnics: RD 989/2015 requires licences and in-person sale; retail record-book duty not confirmed. Not checked: number of armerías, the exact electronic channel/format, whether a Guardia Civil portal already does the filing, collectors' duties.

coverage.category: 32. Autónomo tax and Social Security calendars: RETA income-based contributions regularisation, modelos 303/130 (country-specific)
coverage.found: The RETA regularisation (RD-ley 13/2022) is done by the Seguridad Social crossing its data with the Hacienda income figures, so the autonomo files nothing; only the optional bi-monthly base changes (up to 6 per year) are actioned. Cycles: 2024 income regularised early 2026; 2025 income paid by about 31 Oct 2026 (Billeo; dates inconsistent across sources). Calculators and guides already exist from Infoautónomos, Billeo, Declarando, Legalitas. No mandatory filing found for a software product; generic accounting/tax filing is out of scope.

coverage.category: 33. Municipal licences and registers for small premises: bars and restaurants (APPCC, allergens, terraces, licences) (country-specific)
coverage.found: Duties: APPCC self-control (Reg. 852/2004 art. 5; RD 1021/2022 art. 20), allergen information (Reg. 1169/2011), regional food-establishment register, municipal licencia de actividad and annual terrace authorisation. Terrace renewal is municipal and fragmented: Valladolid publishes a yearly window, usually Q1 (31 Mar 2025); Gijón renews de oficio for 2026; Madrid's decree of 28 Jan 2026 created a terraces commission with automatic renewal for older authorisations. APPCC record apps already exist (Alcomo HACCP, Andy APPCC, EasyQ, Emerson/Copeland sensors). Not checked: SGAE/AGEDI music fees, noise/aforo records, tasa de basuras, number of bars.

coverage.category: 34. Agriculture and livestock small-operator mandates: SITRAN/REGA/REMO, livestock libro de registro, CUE/SIEX, REGFER (country-specific; also touches 6 and 14)
coverage.found: Livestock: REGA covers over 900,000 holdings (RD 479/2004); movements go through REMO (RD 728/2007), which the regional administrations feed; RD 787/2023 unified identification and traceability and requires every holding to keep an up-to-date libro de registro in the format approved by the region (Valencia approved its format by Orden 8/2025 of 6 Jun). No small-holder libro-de-registro app found in one search (competitor coverage not exhaustive). Crops: RD of 18 Nov 2025 postponed the digital phytosanitary notebook (CUE) to 1 Jan 2027; holdings of 5 ha or less (irrigation up to 1 ha) are exempt; MAPA offers a free CUE; fertilisation records may be paper or digital (RD 1051/2022). REGFER registration (art. 18; Orden APA/1226/2025 of 27 Oct) falls on fertiliser makers, importers, distributors and advisers, not farmers. A BOE of 8 Jul 2026 (BOE-A-2026-14762) concerns livestock reproductive products and was not opened.

coverage.category: 35. Employer-side labour and prevention duties for micro-firms: Ley 2/2023 whistleblowing channel, Plan de Igualdad, registro retributivo, PRL self-assumption (country-specific; also touches 26)
coverage.found: Ley 2/2023: internal channel mandatory at 50 or more workers since 1 Dec 2023 (fines quoted at EUR 600,000 or EUR 1m, unverified, art. 65); cheap SaaS exists (Cedesa Lapsowork EUR 299.99+VAT per year, EQS, Atico34, softwaredoit). One blog mentions an AIPI notification form active Feb 2026 and a 10 Apr 2026 deadline; unverified. Plan de Igualdad is mandatory from 50 workers under RD 901/2020 with fines of EUR 7,501-225,018 under LISOS; registro retributivo (RD 902/2020) applies to all firms. PRL: owner may self-assume prevention under art. 11 RSP (sources conflict: fewer than 6 workers vs up to 25 with one workplace; excludes Annex I activities; health surveillance still needs an external service). Directive (EU) 2023/970 transposition status unchecked.

result.competitor: There is a free state tool: operators enter the annual statistics in the ministry's REGFER application. Searches for 'REGFER + ERP/software/programa' found no commercial product that prepares or exports the REGFER statistics. Sector ERPs for agro-input and pesticide dealers exist, such as ASEST's ERP for pesticides and agrochemicals, and they hold the sales data needed for the aggregate. Whether any of them exports REGFER statistics was not verified. The neighbouring pesticide duty (RETO) already has a free ministry system that accepts uploads from ERPs.
result.duty: Under RD 1051/2022 art. 18 and Orden APA/1226/2025 (BOE 3 Nov 2025), shops and other operators that put fertiliser on sale must register in REGFER. Shops go in Section 3 (distributors), and the Andalucía FAQ, as quoted in search summaries, says retail shops count as distributors whether they sell wholesale or retail. Operators already active had to register by 1 Jul 2026; new ones must apply at least 1 month before starting. Each operator registers once but must list all points of sale and stores, and renews every 3 years. Registered operators file annual statistics (the 'Estadísticas Anuales' model) before 31 March for the previous year, first for 2026 data. Sales are split into sales to other registered agents (national total) and sales to end users (by province), and filed in the ministry's REGFER application after the region authorises the user. Penalties were not found (not_reached). The ministry's draft-order PDF returned HTTP 503 and the Andalucía PDF could not be read, so the order's text was not checked directly.
result.market: No published count of REGFER registrants was found. A rough proxy is the ROPO pesticide supplier sector plus garden centres and co-operative shops, likely a few thousand to roughly 10,000 points of sale across Spain. This is an unverified estimate, not a register figure.
result.reason: The duty is real and national. RD 1051/2022 art. 18 and Orden APA/1226/2025 require retail shops that sell fertiliser to register in REGFER Section 3, with 1 Jul 2026 as the deadline for operators already active. Every registered operator must then file annual production and sales statistics before 31 March, starting with 2026 data (so 31 Mar 2027). This is a national rule, not only a Castilla y León procedure. Searches found no dedicated product. But filing is a once-a-year aggregate in the ministry's free REGFER application, renewal is every 3 years, and an agro-shop ERP can produce the totals. There is no per-sale record duty like RETO for pesticides. I found no penalty or shop count. Pain and willingness to pay are low; it works best as a feature of a RETO/ROPO tool.

result.competitor: The free channel is the euskadi.eus sede: a 4-step web form with an e-ID signature. No web service, XML spec or bulk upload was found. Spanish searches for "programa gestión tienda compraventa libro de policía móviles", for Ertzaintza XML or web-service specs, and for Policia Nacional apps returned no Spanish product that files these reports. Only generic US consignment POS tools came up (The Consignment Shop, Ricochet, ConsignCloud, SecondLoop). ORONET is known only for gold (K28), and I did not check whether it covers phones.
result.duty: Basque Country: Orden of 25 June 2020 from the Consejera de Seguridad (BOPV no. 130, 3 July 2020). It replaced the Orden of 24 July 2019, and its annex was amended by the Orden of 23 July 2020. It applies to anyone who buys, sells, pawns or repairs used goods for profit in the Basque Country, including used mobile phones. Covered businesses must register the shop on the euskadi.eus sede and keep the data for 2 years. Each acquisition or receipt must be reported to the Ertzaintza within 24 hours, electronically through the sede, with operation data, the seller's name, surnames and date of birth, and the object's brand, model and IMEI. In-person reporting is allowed only as an exception the Ertzaintza grants case by case. The legal basis is LO 4/2015 art. 25.1. The order text does not state penalties (not verified). Outside the Basque Country, I found only LO 4/2015 art. 25.1 plus the old state rules (a 1989 ministerial order and a 1924 royal order). I found no electronic-reporting rule for the Policia Nacional or the Mossos (not reached).
result.market: Not verified. No register count of obligated establishments was found, and the registration page gives no figure. My rough guess is low thousands of second-hand, phone and repair shops in the Basque Country, but no source supports that number. Catalan press shows Mossos raids on phone resale shops (22 inspected in Raval at once), but I found no Catalan reporting rule.
result.reason: The duty is real but only confirmed for the Basque Country. The Orden of 25 June 2020 replaced the 2019 order, and its annex was amended in July 2020. It requires used-goods, phone, electronics and bazaar shops, and repairers, to report every acquisition or receipt to the Ertzaintza within 24 hours through the euskadi.eus electronic office. Each report includes seller ID, brand, model and IMEI. That is frequent, per-transaction pain. The only channel found is the free sede web form. No bulk upload, web service, format spec or third-party tool was found, so a tool that captures ID and IMEI and pre-fills the filing is plausible. The weaknesses are that it covers one region, the market is small and price-sensitive, and many shops are informal. It is unclear whether the state can automate filing, and no rules were found for other regions.

result.competitor: Four Spanish-language searches found no Spanish vertical F-gas logbook product. Found: generic field-service ERP (STEL Order, which has a page on F-gas handlers; its F-gas features were not checked), foreign tools (Refcom software in the UK, FGASmanager, GoCanvas templates, Edilclima EC771 in Italy), and KoudSmart from the claim (not checked here). Risk: the future state registry may be a free MITECO portal. Regional apps such as Navarra's were not checked.
result.duty: EU Reg 2024/573 has applied directly since 11 Mar 2024: equipment records and leak checks scale with charge (the 3 kg threshold appears in older MITECO notes). RD 115/2017 still requires certified companies and staff. A MITECO note lists logbooks for each piece of equipment and for each authorised company. MITECO is preparing a new Royal Decree to replace RD 115/2017, plus an Order for a centralised electronic registry. The consultation ran 9-24 Sep 2026 and the page now says closed. AEPD report 002/2026 covers the draft decree (stated novelties: certificate publicity, mandatory refresher courses, centralised registry, mandatory training programmes). Neither text is final, and the data and frequency the registry will require are not known. Madrid's annual 'Libro de gestión de refrigerantes' filing (due by 31 Mar; Decreto 138/2011 IF-17) is marked Finalizado. Penalties: not checked.
result.market: Not found. No national count of authorised F-gas companies turned up. Certification is handled by each region's industry service and the companies are listed in the MITECO GASFLUOR unified registry (count not reached). Likely thousands to low tens of thousands of HVAC-R installer firms, but this is unverified.
result.reason: The claim holds up as reported, but the main duty is not settled yet. MITECO ran a pre-drafting consultation from 9 to 24 September 2026 on an Order for a centralised electronic registry. The Order would replace the art. 7 RD 115/2017 registry and Orden TEC/544/2019. There is no draft text, so the data installers must file and the dates are unknown. Search snippets of the consultation PDF point to registry sections on certificates and authorised firms and to tying pre-charged equipment sales to an authorised installer. Nothing says it adds a log of each service visit. Equipment and leak-check records already exist under EU Reg 2024/573. Madrid's annual refrigerant-book filing (Decreto 138/2011, IF-17) shows as closed. I found no Spanish vertical tool, only generic field-service ERPs and UK/Italian tools. The state registry could also end up free.

result.competitor: The core job (downloading, archiving and checking for infractions) is already done by an established category of products, and those tools work for vans as well as trucks. Spanish vendors include Dahuca Soluciones' Tacho2Safe, a USB download device with software for analysing infractions, and Tadig, a Spanish company that specialises in tachograph analysis. Teltonika sells TachoSync, a remote-download service for vans billed per use, and TachoWeb, which reads the Spanish TGD format and costs roughly EUR 550 to 5,200 a year from resellers. Geotab offers remote download, infraction analysis and alerts for download deadlines and card expiry, and Michelin Connected Fleet is also active in Spain. Abroad, OPTAC3 charges about GBP 1 per driver per week, which shows that per-driver pricing small enough for an owner-driver already exists. The claim's gap, a low-cost standalone tool for one-van owners, is at most a pricing and marketing niche, not missing capability. Any solo founder would compete against all of these.
result.duty: The duty is real and has been in force since 1 Jul 2026. Under Reg. (EU) 2020/1054, which amends Reg. 165/2014 and 561/2006 and applies directly in Spain, vans and van-plus-trailer combinations over 2.5 t and up to 3.5 t MMA that carry goods for hire on international trips or cabotage must fit a G2V2 smart tachograph and use a driver card. There is no general transition period. Vans used only on domestic routes are exempt, and the exemptions in Art. 3(aa) and 3(ha) of 561/2006 still apply. I did not confirm the 28/90-day download cycles or the 56-day card rule in this session; they come from 165/2014 and the claim, not from a source I opened. The Spanish fine is unclear: motor16 reports both EUR 2,000 (citing the DGT, for not fitting the tachograph) and 'up to 200 euros' in a separate article. One provider cites EUR 2,001 plus immobilisation for driving without a compliant tachograph, and general tachograph sanctions run from EUR 100 to 6,000. Fenadismer complains that the European Commission still has not issued an interpretive guide, so enforcement differs between member states.
result.market: I found no Spanish figure for vans in scope. Searches of trans.info and other trade press returned no national count. Only vans of 2.5 to 3.5 t doing international work or cabotage are affected, which in Spain is probably a few thousand operators at most and is not quantified here. The Spanish licencia comunitaria register for light vehicles would be the right source but was not reached. A Kienzle survey, from Germany rather than Spain, found that about a third of affected fleets had not adapted by the deadline. Trans.info reports that the tachograph makes van transport up to 80% more expensive, which squeezes how much these operators can spend.
result.reason: The duty is real, mandatory and recurring, with high fines. But the core job (downloading, archiving and checking infractions) is a mature, crowded category in Spain. Tacho2Safe (Dahuca), Tadig, TachoWeb and TachoSync (Teltonika), Geotab and Michelin already do it, and they are sold through tachograph installers and gestorías that already serve hauliers. The buyers in scope are a narrow group (international and cabotage van operators only) with no published Spanish count, and many are probably foreign-based. They are price-squeezed, and an owner-driver often has little to analyse beyond one card. That leaves no clear gap beyond price, so distribution would depend on installers who already bundle these services.
